nodes.name: Epoxide Gelation
nodes.procedure: A Cu-Co oxide precursor (CuCo-OP) was synthesized via an epoxide gelation method, forming a nanoparticle-assembled 3D architecture.
nodes.source_text: First, a Cu-Co oxide precursor (CuCo-OP) was synthesized via an epoxide gelation method, forming a nanoparticle-assembled 3D architecture (Figure S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Electrochemical Reconstruction
nodes.procedure: The CuCo-OP precursor underwent in situ electrochemical reconstruction under NO3RR conditions to form the Ov-Co(OH)2/Cu heterostructures. The applied reduction current critically governs Ov concentration, as unambiguously corroborated by quantitative XPS analysis showing that galvanostatic electroreduction (-200 to -1200 mA cm⁻²) progressively elevates Ov content in Ov-Co(OH)2/Cu from 16.9% to 22.6%. All Ov-Co(OH)2/Cu catalysts referenced herein were fabricated at -800 mA cm⁻² current density.
nodes.source_text: In the second stage, the CuCo-OP precursor underwent in situ electrochemical reconstruction to form the Ov-Co(OH)2/Cu heterostructures... The sample prepared at -800 mA cm⁻² exhibits moderate Ov content (18.0%)

nodes.name: Monocomponent Cu Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Cu catalyst exhibits homologous structural evolution pathway under electrochemical reconstruction, as verified by SEM and XRD results.
nodes.source_text: For monocomponent catalysts, Cu and Ov-Co(OH)2 exhibit homologous structural evolution pathways under electrochemical reconstruction, as verified by SEM and XRD results (Figures S5 and S6, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Monocomponent Ov-Co(OH)2 Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ov-Co(OH)2 catalyst exhibits homologous structural evolution pathway under electrochemical reconstruction, as verified by SEM and XRD results. A clear Ov signal is also observed in the O 1s spectra of Ov-Co(OH)2 with an Ov content quantified at 20.9%.
nodes.source_text: For monocomponent catalysts, Cu and Ov-Co(OH)2 exhibit homologous structural evolution pathways under electrochemical reconstruction... A clear Ov signal is also observed in the O 1s spectra of Ov-Co(OH)2 (Figure S6f, Supporting Information), with an Ov content quantified at 20.9%.

nodes.name: Control Sample Preparation
nodes.procedure: A control sample (Co(OH)2/Cu) was prepared by physically mixing commercial Cu2Cl(OH)3 and Co(OH)2 in a 1:1 mol ratio.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, we prepared a control sample (Co(OH)2/Cu) by physically mixing commercial Cu2Cl(OH)3 and Co(OH)2 in a 1:1 mol ratio.

nodes.characterization_summary: CuCo-OP precursor shows Cu2Cl(OH)3 (PDF#No. 87-0679) as primary crystalline phase with broadened peaks indicating amorphous components.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns identify Cu2Cl(OH)3 (PDF#No. 87-0679) as the primary crystalline phase, while broadened diffraction peaks suggest coexisting amorphous components (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM resolves lattice fringes with d-spacing of 0.223 nm corresponding to (024) plane of Cu2Cl(OH)3 in CuCo-OP precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) images further resolve distinct lattice fringes with a d-spacing of 0.223 nm corresponding to the (024) plane of Cu2Cl(OH)3 (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS reveals Cu and Co species predominantly in +2 oxidation state in CuCo-OP precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis reveals that both Cu and Co species predominantly exist in +2 oxidation state (Figure 1c,d).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals formation of 300-400 nm nanosheet array morphology in Ov-Co(OH)2/Cu after reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After reconstruction, SEM images reveal the formation of 300-400 nm nanosheet array (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM identifies lattice spacings of 0.212 nm for Cu(111) and 0.147 nm for Co(OH)2(111) in Ov-Co(OH)2/Cu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HR-TEM images identify distinct lattice spacings of 0.212 and 0.147 nm corresponding to Cu (111) and Co(OH)2 (111), respectively (Figure 1f,g).

nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns exhibit characteristic peaks with Cu (PDF#85-1326) and Co(OH)2 (PDF#74-1057), demonstrating the reduction of Cu2Cl(OH)3 and the formation of a crystalline Co(OH)2 phase (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms uniform spatial distribution of Cu, Co, and O across Ov-Co(OH)2/Cu nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS mapping confirms uniform spatial distribution of Cu, Co, and O across the Ov-Co(OH)2/Cu nanosheets (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Cu 2p3/2 and 2p1/2 binding energies at 932.2 eV and 952.1 eV indicate Cu0/1+ species in Ov-Co(OH)2/Cu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Ov-Co(OH)2/Cu, the Cu 2p3/2 and 2p1/2 binding energies observed at 932.2 and 952.1 eV, respectively (Figure 1c), are attributed to Cu0/1+ species.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS deconvolution resolves Ov at 532.2 eV (18.0% concentration), surface water at 533.3 eV, and metal-hydroxyl at 531.2 eV in Ov-Co(OH)2/Cu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Deconvolution of O 1s spectra resolves three components: surface-adsorbed water (533.3 eV), oxygen vacancy (Ov) (532.2 eV), and metal-hydroxyl groups (531.2 eV) (Figure 1j).

When the potential was gradually applied from OCP to -0.5 V versus RHE, the Cu (II) pre-edge feature diminished... The metallic Cu was steadily retained across -0.1 to -0.5 V versus RHE (Figure 2a).
